title: lopdf has a stack overflow via deeply nested PDF objects
description: lopdf versions prior to 0.42.0 contain a stack overflow vulnerability in the PDF parser due to unbounded recursion when processing deeply nested PDF arrays or dictionaries. A crafted PDF with around 10,000 levels of nested arrays in the Catalog can cause the parser to exhaust the call stack and abort the process with SIGABRT, resulting in a denial of service. This vulnerability does not cause a panic that can be caught, making it effective for crashing services that parse untrusted PDFs. The issue is fixed in lopdf version 0.42.0 by enforcing a maximum object-nesting depth.
aiSummary: The lopdf library's Document::load_mem function and related entry points parse nested PDF arrays and dictionaries using recursion without a limit on nesting depth. A maliciously crafted PDF with approximately 10,000 nested array levels in the Catalog's /X entry causes the parser to exhaust the call stack, triggering a SIGABRT and crashing the process. This stack overflow results in a denial of service against applications using lopdf to parse untrusted PDF input. The vulnerability affects lopdf versions before 0.42.0 and is resolved by introducing a maximum nesting depth limit in the parser to prevent unbounded recursion.
aiImpact: An attacker can cause a denial of service by submitting a small (~21 KB) crafted PDF file with deeply nested arrays, crashing any service that uses lopdf versions prior to 0.42.0 for PDF parsing. There is no impact on confidentiality or integrity, only availability is affected.
